profile: P150 (one Blackhole P300 chip as N150 mesh)

code.after: final stage code (batched prefill with shape-stable groups and slot-row assembly, expert-sorted MoE prefill, M-independent prefill numerics, device sampler ceiling 32); commit recorded in work_log.md

named_limitations: Decode traces are still released and recaptured on execution-width changes, slot remaps, host-mode decode, after a prefill that compiled new programs (first-seen single-row lengths and chunk continuations), and on every sampling-spec key miss (greedy/sampled switches and request-seed changes); the mixed-shape trace reuse check therefore fails and first-seen long chunked prompts pay compile time in TTFT (open item, trace lifetime redesign excluded from this resume). Final server release reasons: prefill_program_cache_growth 19, slot_remap 16, host_sampling_prefill 10, batch_shape_change 3 (49 captures; no sampling-spec key miss in that run, 27 on the 27c84d5e4d server).
Prefills below 512 rows keep the expert-union MoE path; the sorted path is bit-identical but not faster there.
The expert-sorted MoE prefill synchronizes the host once per layer to read the routing (about 2.6 ms of layout work per layer at 2048 rows).
Greedy decode differs between the batch-1 execution and the 32-slot lane (different DRAM-sharded decode program configs); each width is self-consistent. Pre-existing, not changed here.

The engine admits the first request of a client burst in a prefill step of its own, so a burst of N short prompts forms a batched group of N - 1 rows; the 32x128 burst over the 2048-token prefill budget splits into 16 + 15 (+1) row groups.
The device sampler draws from 32 candidates per user (ttnn.sampling tile width); max_device_top_k is 32 and stochastic requests with top_k 33..64 use the plugin's host sampler.
